pairs.subject: test-harness
pairs.evidence: src/lib/harness/verifier.ts:131 The '0 means pass' check only runs inside the catch branch, but every custom gate is a `grep ... | wc -l` pipeline that exits 0 (probed: a 51-line count exits 0). So runGate takes the success branch and reports every typography, i18n and notification audit as passed whatever the count, and the final report (orchestrator.ts:318) publishes those passes.

techniques.evidence: src/lib/harness/__tests__/verifier.test.ts:88 The emitted shell pipeline is checked against a mocked execSync that throws, and the real reader (sh) never throws on `| wc -l`. The shell is available and cheap, but the oracle never runs it.

src/lib/harness/__tests__/verifier.test.ts:119 'still reads a zero-count custom gate as a pass' pins a decision that real commands never reach, because the pipeline's exit is wc's 0. The test is green while every nonzero count also passes.
src/lib/harness/__tests__/verifier.test.ts:12 Unit tests inherit no machine state because child_process is stubbed. That same stub is why the reader is never consulted.
src/lib/harness/verifier.ts:37 The module wires `npm run test -- --run` as one required gate and owns no partition of its own. Lane design is the repo's, not this context's.

pairs.registryProposal: assert-through-the-reader could name shell pipeline exit semantics (the exit status is the last stage's, so `| wc -l` always exits 0) as a third shape. It is the commonest way a count-gate's verdict detaches from its count.
